<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="77.125.106.121" /></noinclude><section begin="par100" />{{GHGmargin-letter|100|i}}
'''4.''' A number of forms standing in very close relation to the demonstrative pronoun may be regarded as primitive adverbs, since they arise directly from a combination of demonstrative sounds. Some of these have subsequently suffered great mutilation, the extent of which, however, can now very rarely be ascertained with certainty. Such are e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָז|translate=then}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה|translate=here}} (according to Barth, ''Sprachwiss. Abhandlungen'', p. 16, formed from the two demonstrative elements ''hin'' and ''na''), {{GHGheb|text=כֵּן}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּ֫כָה|translate=thus}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֵיכָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽיכָכָה}}, ''how?''), {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ|translate=only}}, {{GHGheb|text=אָכֵן|translate=truly}} (on all these adverbs, see the Lexicon), and especially the interrogative {{GHGheb|text=הֲ}} (''Hē interrogativum''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹא}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲלֹה}}) ''nonne?'', {{GHGheb|text=הֲגַם|translate=num etiam?}} This ''Hē interrogativum'' is perhaps shortened from {{GHGheb|text=הַל}}, which is still used in Arabic, and, according to the view of a certain school of Masoretes, occurs also in Hebrew in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=6}}.<ref>The separation of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} at the beginning of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=6}}, expressly noticed by Qimḥi (ed. Rittenb., p. 40 b) as an unique instance, is perhaps a protest against admitting a particle {{GHGheb|text=הַל}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|k}}
The {{GHGheb|text=ה}} interrogative takes—(1) ''Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ'' generally before non-gutturals (even before {{GHGheb|text=ר}}), with a firm vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֲשַׂ֫מְתָּ|translate=hast thou set}}? see the interrogative clause, {{GHGpar|150|c}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַיִּיטַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=10|verse=19}} is an exception).

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|l}}
(2) Before a consonant with {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, usually {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} without a following {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַֽבְרָכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=38}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=31|hidebook=1}}; less frequently (in about ten passages), {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} with a following {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַבְּדֶרֶךְ|translate=num in via}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=20|verse=30}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַלְּבֶן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=6}}; even in {{GHGheb|text=ר}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=6|verse=32}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|m}}
(3) Before gutturals, not pointed with either {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} or {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}}, it takes {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאֵלֵךְ|translate=shall I go}}?, {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאַתָּה|translate=num tu}}?, {{GHGheb|text=הַאִם|translate=num si}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאֶרְצֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=1|verse=13}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=31}} read {{GHGheb|text=הַֽאַתֶּם}} (not {{GHGheb|text=הָֽא׳}}), likewise {{GHGheb|text=הַ}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=12|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=11}}.—In {{GHGheb|text=הָאִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=16|verse=22}}, the Masora intends the article; read {{GHGheb|text=הַאִישׁ}}, and cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=19}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=21}} read {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֹלָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֲיֹרֶדֶת}}; the article is a correction due to doctrinal considerations.

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|n}}
(4) The {{GHGheb|text=ה}} takes {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} before gutturals pointed with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} or (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=9}} ff.) {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאָמוּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶאָֽנֹכִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶהָֽיְתָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽהָשֵׁב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=5}} (cf. the analogous instances in {{GHGpar|22|c}}, {{GHGpar|35|k}}, {{GHGpar|63|k}}). The place of this interrogative particle is always at the beginning of the clause [but see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=15}}, where one or more words are prefixed for emphasis].

{{GHGmargin-letter|100|o}}
'''5.''' Some adverbs occur also in connexion with suffixes, thus {{GHGheb|text=יֶשְׁךָ|translate=thou art there}}, 3rd sing. masc. {{GHGheb|text=יֶשְׁנוֹ}}<ref>This form, which occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=8}}, is textually very doubtful, and cannot be supported by the equally doubtful {{GHGheb|text=קָבְנוֹ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=קֻבֶּ֫נּוּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}. Most probably, with Stade, ''Gramm.'', § 370 b, and P. Haupt, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}} Numbers, p. 57, line 37, we should read {{GHGheb|text=יֵשֶׁ֫נּוּ}}.</ref> (but see note below), 2nd plur. masc. {{GHGheb|text=יֶשְׁבֶם}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נִּי|translate=I am not}}, 2nd sing. {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽינְךָ}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֵךְ}}, 3rd sing. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נּוּ}}, fem. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינֶ֫נָּה}}, 2nd plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽינְכֶם}}, 3rd plur. masc. {{GHGheb|text=אֵינָם}}.—Also {{GHGheb|text=עוֹדֶ֫נִּי|translate=I am yet}} ({{GHGheb|text=עוֹדִי}} only in {{GHGheb|text=בְּעוֹדִי}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֵֽעוֹדִי}}), {{GHGheb|text=עֽוֹדְךָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוֹדָךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוֹדֵ֫ינוּ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=17}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGheb|text=עוֹדֶ֫ינָה}}<section end="par100" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
